# Task 43: skin-matched "Picture this" drawing while the picture loads

Repo martinmw13/LectorIA-meta, worktree /workspace/wt-43, branch `picture-this-draw` (from latest main). Read AGENTS.md first and follow every repo rule (co-author trailer via the hook, 5k-token file-size hook, check:secrets, check:isolation). No paid API calls, do not run `next start`, do not touch data/, do not touch server/ or app/image-style.ts. Never stop to ask; make reasonable calls and note them. First write the design in docs/tasks/43-picture-this-draw.md (short), then implement.

## Reference prototype (approved by the user)
`.muse-ref/index.html` (+ `.muse-ref/assets/`) is a standalone prototype, not part of the repo (never commit `.muse-ref/`). It shows 6 variants; the user chose THREE:
- engraving skin -> variant **eB "Etching needle, oval vignette"** (needle scratches an oval plate + contours, then fine cross-hatching; picture comes up sepia, then full colour).
- watercolor skin -> variant **wA "Blooming washes"** (brush dabs, colour blooms bleed outward; picture comes in as a wash spreading from the middle, blur to sharp).
- ink skin -> variant **iA "Ballpoint doodle"** (blue ballpoint doodles contours, then zigzag shading; picture pops in blue ink, then colour).
Port those three faithfully (paper, tool glyph riding the stroke tip, strokes, SVG filters, reveal), as a React client component using SVG + requestAnimationFrame (no new dependencies). The prototype's Oz house/cyclone paths are fine as the stand-in sketch. Note the prototype's `Run.cut` getter: the drawing must stop wherever it is the moment the picture arrives.

## Behaviour
- When the user clicks Picture this, the image slot shows the blank skin paper IMMEDIATELY (no spinner), and the skin's tool starts drawing on it, looping layers until /api/images answers (~20 s). Applies to the left image pane (app/folio/image-pane.tsx, `loading` phase) and to inline figures (app/folio/inline-figures.tsx, `loading` phase): share one component.
- Never block on animation length: the instant the real image is ready, abort the drawing at whatever point it reached and reveal the image with a SHORT skin reveal (total <= ~900 ms; engraving: brief sepia then colour; watercolor: quick bloom from the centre; ink: quick pop). After the reveal only the image remains; nothing keeps moving. If the reveal can't be done cleanly within the existing ready-phase markup, a plain crossfade (<= 500 ms) from drawing to image is acceptable. Errors still show the existing error + retry.
- Status copy under/inside the slot, warm English, e.g. engraving "Etching the plate…", watercolor "Letting the colours bloom…", ink "Doodling your scene…", plus a small "Usually about twenty seconds". Never use the word "Generated". Keep `role="status"` for a11y. Replace PICTURE_COPY.loading usage accordingly (keep it if still used elsewhere).
- prefers-reduced-motion: no drawing animation; show the variant's static `still()` drawing with the tool resting, then a <= 200 ms opacity swap to the image.
- Picture this stays absent on chapter covers (`bare`) as today.

## Skin selection
A skin seam (data-skin attribute on <html>, `?skin=` param) is being built on another branch and is NOT in main. Add a tiny helper (e.g. app/folio/picture-skin.ts) `pictureSkin(): "engraving" | "watercolor" | "ink"` that reads `document.documentElement.dataset.skin`, else the `?skin=` URL param, else returns "engraving"; unknown values (including "default") -> "engraving". SSR-safe. Unit test it.

## The Picture this button (pane pill and the scene/chapter pair)
- Remove the box/frame: no border, no pill background. The illustration IS the button: a small skin-matched drawing (see the prototype's BTN_ART for engraving/watercolor/ink, Meta blue #0866FF accents) plus the label text, and it must still read clearly as clickable (cursor pointer, accent-coloured label, visible hover change, focus-visible ring kept).
- Animate ONLY on hover and on click/state change (e.g. a tiny press/glint/wiggle like the prototype's engrave-press, wet-press, wiggle keyframes). No idle loops anywhere on the button. Remove the infinite `pane-pulse` loading animation. Under prefers-reduced-motion: no button animation.
- Light mode, Meta blue (use existing --color-accent tokens), never purple. Keep labels "Picture this scene" / "Picture the chapter".

## Tests
- picture-skin helper test.
- A jsdom test (pattern: app/folio/use-pictures.test.tsx, createRoot + act, no new deps) that renders the loading slot, asserts the paper SVG and status render immediately, then flips to ready and asserts the image is rendered without waiting for the drawing to finish (fake timers ok; stub requestAnimationFrame / matchMedia / SVG getTotalLength as needed).

## Done when
`npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run check:secrets`, `npm run check:size`, `npm run check:isolation` and `npm run build` all pass. Keep every file under the size hook limit (split paths/data into their own module). Commit in sensible steps with clear messages; the hook adds the trailer. Add one short line for task 43 to BUILT_DURING_HACKATHON.md. Do not push.

---

# Anti-Slop: Frontend DON'Ts

What NOT to do when designing a UI or page. This is a filter, not a style; it never prescribes a look. Stacking several of the below is what reads as AI-made on sight. Adaptive, so if the user or another skill asks for something specific, do that instead; these are defaults, not overrides.

- purple / indigo / violet accent, or a purple-to-blue hero gradient (the top AI tell)
- `bg-clip-text` gradient headline text
- cream (`#faf8f4`) as the whole-page background
- aurora blobs / glowing colored shadows, or an identical glow on every card
- Inter everywhere, or Geist / Space Grotesk / Instrument Serif / Roboto / Arial as your only identity
- gray-400 / gray-500 body text
- one font weight and size throughout (no hierarchy)
- tracked all-caps micro-kickers above every section
- centered hero of eyebrow pill + headline + two CTAs
- the identical 3-card feature grid with a lucide icon in a rounded square
- an 8+ word, 48px+ headline that says nothing
- bento grid for everything
- the same eyebrow-headline-3cards section repeated back to back
- `rounded-2xl`, or any single radius, on every element
- glassmorphism blur + border + shadow on every surface
- `hover:scale-105` lift on cards
- emoji as feature icons (🚀 ⚡ ✨ 🎯 💡)
- left-border accent cards, a colored border on a rounded element, or cards nested inside cards
- fade-up / slide-up on everything as it scrolls in
- motion that ignores `prefers-reduced-motion`
- scribbly hand-drawn SVG mascots with no purpose

</skill-body>
</read-skill-result>

# Anti-Slop: Frontend DON'Ts

What NOT to do when designing a UI or page. This is a filter, not a style; it never prescribes a look. Stacking several of the below is what reads as AI-made on sight. Adaptive, so if the user or another skill asks for something specific, do that instead; these are defaults, not overrides.

- purple / indigo / violet accent, or a purple-to-blue hero gradient (the top AI tell)
- `bg-clip-text` gradient headline text
- cream (`#faf8f4`) as the whole-page background
- aurora blobs / glowing colored shadows, or an identical glow on every card
- Inter everywhere, or Geist / Space Grotesk / Instrument Serif / Roboto / Arial as your only identity
- gray-400 / gray-500 body text
- one font weight and size throughout (no hierarchy)
- tracked all-caps micro-kickers above every section
- centered hero of eyebrow pill + headline + two CTAs
- the identical 3-card feature grid with a lucide icon in a rounded square
- an 8+ word, 48px+ headline that says nothing
- bento grid for everything
- the same eyebrow-headline-3cards section repeated back to back
- `rounded-2xl`, or any single radius, on every element
- glassmorphism blur + border + shadow on every surface
- `hover:scale-105` lift on cards
- emoji as feature icons (🚀 ⚡ ✨ 🎯 💡)
- left-border accent cards, a colored border on a rounded element, or cards nested inside cards
- fade-up / slide-up on everything as it scrolls in
- motion that ignores `prefers-reduced-motion`
- scribbly hand-drawn SVG mascots with no purpose

# Durable Test Collateral

Verification is part of the delivered project when it can prevent the same
behavior from breaking again. Use the project's existing framework and
conventions.

Loading this skill does not mean the current turn asked for the change. While you
are still investigating — explaining existing behavior, or answering a design
question the user raised — use commands that only read and leave the repository
unmodified, tests included.

## Scale to the task

Skip the failing-test-first workflow below when the change is tiny and leaves
program logic alone (a typo, a text or style tweak, a config value, or a version
pin), when the work is a throwaway prototype or a standalone one-file script or
page, when the request adds features to a project you created earlier in this
session, or when the user asks for speed or a quick result. A quick direct check
of the changed behavior is enough there; if you add no maintained test, say so in
the report. A user request for tests anywhere in the session, or a
specification that makes tests a deliverable, still applies.

Any other bug fix or behavior change keeps the workflow at its smallest: one
focused failing test, the fix, that test passing, and, when a broad run is
required, one broad run after the final edit. A report that something already
built behaves wrongly is a bug fix, even when it comes with feature requests.

Before a test run that may take more than a minute or two, tell the user in one
line what runs and why. If you poll it, post a short status line between polls;
never poll a long run silently.

## Keep the check with the project

For a bug fix or behavior change, add or update the smallest maintained test in
the repository's normal test layout that exercises the changed behavior. If a
specification makes a reusable suite or test category a deliverable, implement
that suite instead of treating it as private verification.

An inline interpreter command, heredoc, scratch script, temporary-directory
test, demo, or manual probe may help diagnose the problem, but it does not
replace the maintained test. Keep a useful self-authored test unless the user
explicitly asks for a disposable probe.

Do not add a new test framework solely to satisfy this skill. If the repository
has no maintained harness and the request does not require one, disclose when
durable coverage would be disproportionate or infeasible and use the narrowest
honest verification instead.

On a later turn, update the maintained test even when the old suite remains
green and the user does not repeat the test request. Cover the new behavior,
not merely an unrelated cleanup in the test file.

## Prove the maintained check

Observe the authentic failure before the implementation change when it is safe
and runnable. Then make the smallest implementation change and run the focused
maintained test after the final relevant source or test edit.

Do not weaken or delete a real failing test to obtain green. Fix the product,
or explain why the test's expectation is wrong before changing that
expectation. Do not repeat an unchanged check solely to collect evidence.

Run a broad or full suite only when the user, a repository gate, or
proportionate risk requires it, and then once, after the final edit, rather
than after each intermediate edit. A focused regression test comes first; broad
proof does not substitute for missing focused coverage.

Before deciding what a repository gate requires, read what the repository
declares it runs: its CI workflow, its test entry points, and its root-level
scripts listed with hidden entries included. A suite the project itself runs
over this change is a gate, not an optional extra, and a suite that skips
itself when its data is absent is not a green result.

A runner is unavailable only after you tried to make it available. When the
repository ships the command that fetches or builds the missing fixture,
corpus, or toolchain, run that command once and then run the gate. Report the
gate unavailable only when that attempt itself failed, and say what failed.

If the real runner is unavailable but the focused test can still be authored
honestly, leave the focused test in the repository and say it was not run. Do
not fabricate a passing result.
